title: Safety Briefing Canvas + Rollback Decision Tree (prototype)
creator: Arielle Tan
description: Design a compact Safety Briefing Canvas inside Redwood Console that gives operators a single-pane overview before releasing traffic changes. The canvas includes live signal snapshots (latency, error budget, user metrics), a compact ‘what-if’ traffic simulator, and an interactive Rollback Decision Tree that guides engineers through automated and manual rollback options. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during releases and standardize runbook actions for canary / A/B traffic shifts.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Arielle: Initial concept sketches completed. Focus is on a minimal info-dense header, traffic simulator micro-widget, and stepwise rollback decision tree. Linked rough sketches: https://figma.com/file/xxxxx/safety-canvas-rough

2026-03-03 - Elena: Reviewed with PM (Marco Ruiz). PM asked for clear mapping from decision tree nodes to Console actions (e.g., 'scale down variant', 'shift 10% back', 'pause rollout') and audit log entries. Added to next iteration.

2026-03-05 - Design Review: Attendees (PM, 2x Eng, 1x SRE). Engineering flagged data freshness constraints for signal widgets (30s vs 5s) and asked for fallback when metrics are delayed. SRE suggested a reversible ‘emergency freeze’ action in the tree.

2026-03-07 - Usability test: 5 internal engineers ran a 5-minute simulated rollout using the prototype. Key findings: (1) Decision tree language needs to be less ambiguous around 'rollback' vs 'scale back', (2) Simulator should show the expected latency percentile band after traffic shift, (3) Add a keyboard shortcut for 'escalate to on-call'.

2026-03-09 - Engineering notes (ENG-41234): Backend will expose a rollout-intent API and a decision-action endpoint. Need a small schema change to include 'audit_reason' and 'requested_by' fields for UI-initiated rollbacks. Dependency created: ENG-41234.
